Persistent onshore flow, afternoon sea breezes, and a passing trough continue advecting cool marine air that limits inland warming despite the broader seasonal pattern favoring near- or slightly above-average Pacific Northwest temperatures. These local dynamics align closely with the 1991–2020 August climatological mean high of 77°F at Sea-Tac and the absence of strong ridge amplification in recent model runs. Updated NWS briefings or afternoon observation shifts remain the main near-term catalysts ahead of market resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/chongqing/ZUCK.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent model consensus points to a peak temperature near 35–37°C in Chongqing on August 12, 2026, aligning with the market’s heaviest volume on those outcomes.** Subtropical high pressure combined with the city’s mountainous basin topography continues to trap heat and moisture, producing typical midsummer conditions where daytime maxima reach 34–38°C. Official guidance from sources such as the Met Office and regional models currently centers on 36–37°C, while any onshore flow or remnant moisture from nearby tropical systems could cap the reading at 35°C or below. 

Longer-range ensemble spreads show modest upward bias if skies remain mostly clear, but increased cloud cover or scattered showers—common in August—would favor the lower side of the distribution. Historical August extremes in Chongqing frequently exceed 40°C, yet current steering patterns and short-range guidance make 38°C or higher lower-probability events priced accordingly by traders. Updated model runs and local observations over the next 24 hours will determine whether the distribution shifts toward 37°C or settles near 35–36°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: The southwest monsoon, or habagat, remains the dominant driver, sustaining cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms over Metro Manila on August 12 and suppressing peak solar heating. Official PAGASA forecasts indicate daytime highs near 30–32°C amid 60–90% rain chances, aligning with historical August averages around 31°C while recent enhanced monsoon activity from nearby tropical systems has reinforced widespread cloud cover and moisture. These conditions position 30°C as the market leader, with modest upside risk to 31–32°C if breaks in convection allow brief insolation; cooler outcomes would require heavier, prolonged rainfall. Updated model guidance and PAGASA briefings through the 12th will provide the next key inputs for traders assessing resolution thresholds.
